labels.t2:
If the local transaction
fails, a message is sent
to roll back the prepared
message just sent
labels.t3:
Once system A sends the
confirm message, MQ lets
system B consume it
labels.t5:
Calls back an API of
system A and asks: roll
this message back, or
resend a confirm message?
labels.t6:
If system A fails while
sending the confirm message,
the message stays in the
prepared state
labels.t7:
rocketmq automatically polls
all prepared messages
labels.t8:
System B must guarantee
its own idempotency
labels.t9:
It can also record a flag in
redis to show that it has
already processed a message
labels.t10:
It can also create a node in zk
to mean that it has already
processed a certain message. If a
duplicate message arrives, creating
the zk node reports an error
labels._title: Reliable message eventual consistency with RocketMQ
labels._desc: System A sends a prepared message to RocketMQ, then a confirm message once its local transaction succeeds, and RocketMQ lets system B consume it; RocketMQ polls unconfirmed prepared messages and calls system A back, and system B must be idempotent.
